## Pattern

- **[45]** # Hook Shared-Lib Checklist

**Extracted:** 2026-03-01
**Context:** Writing or modifying any hook in ~/.claude/hooks/

## Problem

Hook files repeatedly reimplemented the same utilities locally (stdin reading, slug derivation,
PROJECTS_DIR constant, line trimming) instead of using the shared libs. This caused drift and bugs
when the shared implementation changed.

## Solution

Before writing any logic in a hook, check these two shared libs first:

**`hooks/lib/hookUtils.ts`** exports:
- `readStdin()` — reads stdin fully as string
- `readStdinPassthrough()` — reads stdin and echoes to stdout (Stop hooks)
- `parseHookInput(raw)` — parses JSON, extracts cwd
- `readFileSafe(path)` — returns "" if missing
- `appendLine(path, line)` — append with newline handling
- `trimToLines(content, max)` — keep last N lines

**`hooks/lib/resolveProject.ts`** exports:
- `resolveProject(cwd)` — returns `{ name, projectDir, isNew, registeredPath }`
- `PROJECTS_DIR` — `~/.claude/projects` (use this, don't re-derive)
- `PROJECTS_DIR`, `CLAUDE_DIR`, `REGISTRY_PATH` — all pre-computed constants
- `registerPath(cwd, name)`, `saveRegistry(registry)` — for registration hooks

## Example

```ts
// BAD — reimplementing what hookUtils already has
async function readStdin() {
  let data = "";
  for await (const chunk of Bun.stdin.stream()) data += new TextDecoder().decode(chunk);
  return JSON.parse(data);
}
const PROJECTS_DIR = join(homedir(), ".claude", "projects");

// GOOD — use shared libs
import { readStdin, trimToLines } from "../lib/hookUtils.js";
import { resolveProject, PROJECTS_DIR } from "../lib/resolveProject.js";
```

## When to Use

Every time you create or modify a file in `hooks/`. Run a quick mental checklist:
- Need to read stdin? → `hookUtils.readStdin`
- Need to find the project dir? → `resolveProject(cwd).projectDir`
- Need the projects root? → `PROJECTS_DIR`
- Need to trim a file to N lines? → `trimToLines`
- Need to append a line? → `appendLine` *(claude-config)* `[hooks, claude-code]` ★★★★☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)

- **[44]** # Append-Then-Trim In Memory (Avoid Double File Read)

**Extracted:** 2026-03-01
**Context:** Any code that appends a line to a file and then needs to trim/process the updated content

## Problem

Common anti-pattern: append a line to a file, then immediately re-read the file to process it.
This does unnecessary I/O and can cause TOCTOU issues if the file is written concurrently.

```ts
// BAD — reads file twice
appendFileSync(FILE, newLine);
const lines = readFileSync(FILE, "utf-8").split("\n"); // redundant re-read
if (lines.length > MAX) writeFileSync(FILE, trim(lines));
```

## Solution

Read once before the append. Build the updated content in memory by concatenating the original
content with the new line. Use that for any post-append processing.

```ts
// GOOD — single read, in-memory update
const existing = readFileSync(FILE, "utf-8");
if (!existing.includes(dedupKey)) {
  const newLine = `- new entry\n`;
  appendFileSync(FILE, newLine);

  // Compute updated content in memory — no second read needed
  const updatedLines = (existing + newLine).split("\n");
  if (updatedLines.length > MAX) {
    writeFileSync(FILE, updatedLines.slice(-MAX).join("\n"));
  }
}
```

## When to Use

Any time you see the pattern: `appendFileSync(f, x)` followed by `readFileSync(f)` within
the same function. The re-read is almost always avoidable by keeping the pre-append content
in a variable and concatenating with the new data. `[typescript, file-io, performance]` ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)

## Architecture

- **[69]** - Stack: Next.js 16 (App Router) + RSC + Server Actions — no client-side mutations; SQLite prohibited per BRIEFING.md *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)
- **[70]** - Runtime: Bun exclusively (prohibited: npm, yarn, pnpm, npx) *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)
- **[71]** - DB: PostgreSQL 16 + Prisma ORM — multi-tenant schema (Tenant → User/Alert/Investigation/InvestigationStep/Integration/AuditLog) *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)
- **[72]** - Auth: NextAuth with Prisma adapter; local passwordHash (dev), Entra ID (prod) *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)
- **[73]** - Security: AES-256-GCM (BYOK) for API secrets; PII redaction mandatory in all AI prompts *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)
- **[74]** - AI: Vercel AI SDK (ai + @ai-sdk/anthropic|openai|azure) — orchestrator pattern in lib/ai/ *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)
- **[75]** - UI: Kiranism-style, 6 themes via lib/themes.ts + ThemeProvider, Recharts for charts, TanStack Table for data tables *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)
- **[76]** - RBAC: VIEWER | ANALYST | LEAD | ADMIN roles on User model *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)
- **[77]** - Validation: Zod at every boundary (API, DB, UI) — zero any, strict TypeScript *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)
- **[78]** - Biome for lint/format (not ESLint/Prettier) *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)
- **[79]** - Raw SQL ($queryRaw): use camelCase quoted identifiers ("tenantId", "detectedAt", etc.) — no @map on Alert fields *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)
- **[80]** - Table names: alerts, investigations, investigation_steps (via @@map); column names are camelCase (no @map per-field) *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)
- **[81]** - Azure OpenAI removed from LLM provider UI — Microsoft Azure is Entra/Defender only, not LLM *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)

- **[86]** - HITL mandatory for all "DESTRUCTIVE" remediation actions — no autonomous execution *(ai-soc-assistant)* ★★★☆☆ (conf: 1.00, confirmed: 1x)
